description: Deep Space Learners is a team passionate about AI, Data Science, Machine Learning, and Space Exploration. We aim to use NASA's open data to build innovative solutions. We welcome creative and motivated participants with skills in Python, AI/ML, Web Development, UI/UX Design, Data Visualization, Astronomy, and Research. Join us to learn, collaborate, and explore beyond boundaries! 🌌
summary: The Earth Information Jukebox is an interactive, user-friendly web application designed to make NASA’s vast Earth observation data accessible, engaging, and easy to understand for everyone. Instead of navigating complex scientific datasets, users can browse and select from curated "tracks" or categories—such as climate change, air quality, ocean temperatures, and extreme weather—to explore satellite insights through clear visualizations and simple explanations. By transforming raw NASA data into an intuitive, jukebox-style experience, our solution directly addresses the challenge of bridging the gap between complex space-based science and everyday public awareness. This project is important because it empowers students, educators, and communities to easily understand how our planet is changing and make informed decisions to protect Earth’s future.
details: Earth Information Jukebox is a browser-based data sonification lab that transforms NASA Earth observation visualizations and climate datasets into live, interactive music. Satellite maps and multi-decade temperature records are typically built for the eyes, leaving blind, low-vision, and neurodiverse learners excluded from exploring planetary science. Our web application solves this problem by allowing users to select NASA datasets—such as GISTEMP v4 global temperature anomalies (1880–2026) and NASA SVS Earth visualizations—or upload their own maps, and hear the data in real time with no server or installation required. Using OpenCV.js and Tone.js, the app splits maps into a 16×16 grid and translates brightness, hue, and edge density into musical pitch, rhythm, and stereo panning, alongside keyboard controls, screen-reader support, and written summaries for full accessibility.
